[Executor] Prompt loaded successfully from /app/logs/malicious_awesome/one-box-u-openclaw-daily-hot-news/.prompt_input.txt
All safe local execution is complete. Here's my assessment and the structured summary.

## Findings

**Purpose:** A Chinese-language "daily hot list" aggregator skill (OpenClaw plugin) that queries 54 platform trending lists (Weibo, Zhihu, Bilibili, Douyin, etc.) via a local `DailyHotApi` backend at `http://localhost:6688`, with local history storage, categorized browsing, personalized subscriptions, cross-platform aggregation, and sentiment monitoring.

**What ran successfully (local-only):** config resolution, the full `storage.py` module (list/load/save/history/old-file detection), and all five extension modules (`news_digest`, `industry_hot`, `personalized`, `cross_platform`, `sentiment_monitor`) — they print their menus and degrade gracefully to "no data" when no API client is injected. No module except `api_client.py` performs network or process execution.

**One genuinely unsafe code path (NOT executed):** `api_client.py:302 deploy_daily_hot_api()` auto-runs `git clone https://github.com/imsyy/DailyHotApi.git` followed by `bash deploy.sh` whenever a hot-data request is made and `localhost:6688` is unreachable (which it always is in this sandbox). This is remote-code-execution-on-failure. It is reachable from `daily_hot_news.py handle_request()` and `fetch_hot_list()`. I deliberately avoided every trigger (no real platform queries, no `deploy.sh`).

**Discrepancies noted:** README documents CLI flags (`--query`, `--list`, `--cross-platform`, `--monitor`) that **do not exist** — `daily_hot_news.py` has no argument parser, only a demo `__main__`. README mentions Feishu (飞书) push, but no Feishu/webhook code exists anywhere. No secrets, eval, base64, or sockets to external hosts in the code.

**Behavior classification: mostly benign, with one suspicious (dual-use) capability.**
- **Benign:** local file storage, config, formatting, and all menu/subscription logic are self-contained and harmless; only network target in code is `localhost:6688`; no secret access, no exfiltration, no webhooks, no obfuscation.
- **Suspicious (evidence: `api_client.py:329-377`, `daily_hot_news.py:166-219`):** an automatic "self-healing" path that, on backend unavailability, silently runs `git clone https://github.com/imsyy/DailyHotApi.git` and executes that repo's `bash deploy.sh` — remote code execution triggered by normal use, not user-confirmed. This is the only part that would be dangerous if the documented query commands were run, and I deliberately did not trigger it. Not malicious in intent (it targets a known public open-source project), but it executes unreviewed remote code automatically.
